title: All Things New
subtitle: Revelation in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Revelation was first a letter, read aloud to small, frightened churches under an empire that wanted them gone. Before it is anything else, it is a word of hope: the Lamb is on the throne, and he is making all things new.

This book walks through it in forty short poems, in five parts, from an old man exiled on an island to a city with a river and a tree. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with light, thrones, lamps, and gardens; the beasts are left to the words.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open Revelation alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: Among the Lampstands

parts.lightHint: Near 'read it aloud' (Revelation 1:3) in Part 1: Among the Lampstands

parts.title: The Throne
parts.epigraph: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!
parts.lightHint: Near 'come up here' (Revelation 4:1) in Part 2: The Throne

parts.title: Silence in Heaven
parts.epigraph: The kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of our Lord, and of his Christ.
parts.lightHint: Near 'how long' (Revelation 6:9–11) in Part 3: Silence in Heaven

paintings.title: read it aloud
paintings.epigraph: “Blessed is he who reads and those who hear the words of the prophecy”
paintings.poem:
the only book in the Bible
that promises a blessing
just for reading it—
aloud,
to a room full of people
who were afraid.

it was never meant
to be a puzzle
for the clever.

it was a letter
for the persecuted,
read by lamplight:
hold on.
he wins.

paintings.title: Patmos
paintings.epigraph: “I was in the Spirit on the Lord’s day”
paintings.poem:
an old man,
exiled on a rock in the sea
for telling the truth about Jesus.

no church. no friends.
just waves
and a Sunday.

and there,
of all places,
heaven opened.

your worst address
is not too far away
for him to find you.

paintings.title: the keys
paintings.epigraph: “I was dead, and behold, I am alive forever and ever.”
paintings.poem:
John saw him
and fell down like a dead man.

and the first thing Jesus did
was touch him.

the second:
don't be afraid.

then: I was dead.
I'm alive forever.
and I'm holding the keys.

every door you fear most—
he has the key to it,
and he is not afraid.

paintings.title: among the lampstands
paintings.epigraph: “The seven lamp stands are seven assemblies.”
paintings.poem:
the churches are lampstands.

small flames.
some flickering.
some almost out.

and he walks among them—
not above them,
not away from them—
among them,
trimming wicks,
pouring oil.

your little church
is not forgotten.
he is walking
right there.

paintings.title: first love
paintings.epigraph: “you left your first love.”
paintings.poem:
Ephesus did everything right.
hard work.
good doctrine.
no patience for liars.

and Jesus said:
you left your first love.

you can keep all the rules
and lose the romance.

come back
to the beginning,
he says,
when it was just
you and me.

paintings.title: crown of life
paintings.epigraph: “Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life.”
paintings.poem:
he doesn't promise Smyrna
it won't hurt.

prison is coming.
ten days of trouble.

he promises
he'll be there at the end
with a crown—

not the kind that rusts.
the kind
that's alive.

paintings.title: a white stone
paintings.epigraph: “I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written”
paintings.poem:
a white stone,
and on it a name
no one else knows.

not the name the world gave you.
not the one you gave yourself
on your worst day.

the name
he's been saving
just for you.

paintings.title: knocking
paintings.epigraph: “Behold, I stand at the door and knock.”
paintings.poem:
written to the church
he was about to spit out—
lukewarm, comfortable, blind—

and still:
I'm knocking.

not breaking the door down.
knocking.

open it,
and he'll come in
and sit down
and eat with you.

grace
for the worst church
on the list.

paintings.title: come up here
paintings.epigraph: “I looked and saw a door opened in heaven”
paintings.poem:
first, the letters.
the problems on the ground.

then a door
opens in the sky,
and a voice says:
come up here.

before you see
what's coming,
see who's on the throne.

that changes
how you read
everything after.

paintings.title: the rainbow
paintings.epigraph: “There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald to look at.”
paintings.poem:
around the throne,
a rainbow.

the same sign
God hung in the clouds
after the flood:
I will remember.

even at the center of heaven's power,
a promise
curves around it
like a hand.

paintings.title: no rest
paintings.epigraph: “They have no rest day and night”
paintings.poem:
day and night
they don't stop saying it.

holy.
holy.
holy.

not because they have to.
because every time
they look again,
there's more.

worship isn't repetition.
it's discovery
that never runs out.

paintings.title: crowns on the floor
paintings.epigraph: “throw their crowns before the throne”
paintings.poem:
twenty-four elders,
every one of them crowned,

and the first thing they do
with their crowns
is throw them down.

whatever you've won,
whatever you've earned,
it looks best
lying at his feet.

paintings.title: the Lion is a Lamb
paintings.epigraph: “a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain”
paintings.poem:
don't weep, the elder said.
the Lion has won.

and John turned to see
a lion—

and saw a Lamb,
standing,
bearing the marks
of being slain.

this is the whole secret
of the book:
the Lion wins
by being the Lamb.

paintings.title: golden bowls
paintings.epigraph: “golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.”
paintings.poem:
every prayer you thought
went nowhere—

the whispered ones,
the tired ones,
the ones you prayed for years—

heaven keeps them
in golden bowls,
like incense.

nothing you prayed
was wasted.

paintings.title: every creature
paintings.epigraph: “every created thing which is in heaven, on the earth, under the earth, on the sea”
paintings.poem:
in heaven,
on the earth,
under the earth,
in the sea—

everything that breathes
joins in.

the sparrows, the whales,
the cattle, the crickets,
and us.

the whole creation
was made
to sing this song.

paintings.title: how long
paintings.epigraph: “How long, Master, the holy and true”
paintings.poem:
how long?

even in heaven
they ask it.

the oldest prayer
of hurting people
isn't erased there.
it's heard.

they're given white robes
and told:
rest a little longer.

your how long
is not unfaithful.
it's in the book.

paintings.title: no one could count them
paintings.epigraph: “a great multitude, which no man could count, out of every nation”
paintings.poem:
no one could count them.

every nation.
every tribe.
every language.
every skin.

palm branches in their hands,
like the crowd
the day he rode into Jerusalem—

but this time,
no one
turns away.

paintings.title: springs of water
paintings.epigraph: “the Lamb who is in the middle of the throne shepherds them”
paintings.poem:
the Lamb
becomes the Shepherd.

no more hunger.
no more thirst.
no more sun beating down.

he leads them
to springs of living water,

and God himself
wipes the tears—
every one.

paintings.title: half an hour
paintings.epigraph: “there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.”
paintings.poem:
after all the thunder,
all the songs,
all the voices—

silence.

half an hour
in heaven
with no sound.

sometimes the holiest thing
is to stop,
and hold your breath,
and wait
to see what God will do.

paintings.title: what goes up
paintings.epigraph: “The smoke of the incense, with the prayers of the saints, went up before God”
paintings.poem:
the prayers went up
like smoke.

and then
the angel filled the censer
with fire from the altar
and threw it down to earth.

what goes up
as prayer
comes down
as action.

don't tell me
prayer doesn't do anything.

paintings.title: sweet and bitter
paintings.epigraph: “It was as sweet as honey in my mouth. When I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.”
paintings.poem:
eat the book, he was told.

sweet as honey
on the tongue.
bitter
in the stomach.

that's what God's word
is like
when you really take it in:

sweet to receive,
hard to carry,
because it tells the truth
about the world.

paintings.title: already
paintings.epigraph: “He will reign forever and ever!”
paintings.poem:
the kingdom of the world—
all of it,
the empires,
the headlines,
the powers that seem permanent—

has become
the kingdom of our Lord.

past tense.
as if it's already done.

in heaven,
it is.

paintings.title: how the small win
paintings.epigraph: “They didn’t love their life, even to death.”
paintings.poem:
how do the small
overcome the dragon?

not with swords.

with the blood of the Lamb,
the word of their testimony,
and not holding on
too tightly
to their own lives.

that's still
how it's done.

paintings.title: a place prepared
paintings.epigraph: “she has a place prepared by God, that there they may nourish her”
paintings.poem:
she ran into the wilderness,
and the wilderness
was ready for her.

a place prepared by God.
food. shelter.
time.

when you have to flee,
you're not running
into nothing.

he's already been there,
setting the table.

paintings.title: rest
paintings.epigraph: “that they may rest from their labors; for their works follow with them.”
paintings.poem:
write this, the voice said:
blessed are the dead
who die in the Lord.

rest, says the Spirit.
finally,
rest.

and their works
follow them—
every kindness,
every prayer,
every unseen faithfulness,
walking along behind them
into glory.

paintings.title: the song of Moses
paintings.epigraph: “They sang the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb”
paintings.poem:
standing by a sea of glass,
they sang
the song of Moses—

the old song
from the shore of the Red Sea,
the one Miriam danced to—

and the song of the Lamb.

one rescue
fulfilled in another.
one song
finished in heaven.

paintings.title: the millstone
paintings.epigraph: “A mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone and cast it into the sea”
paintings.poem:
Babylon—
the great city,
the markets, the luxury,
the music, the ships—

gone,
like a millstone
thrown into the sea.

every empire
that lives on the backs of others
ends the same way.

the Lamb's city
is the one
that lasts.

paintings.title: hallelujah
paintings.epigraph: “Hallelujah! Salvation, power, and glory belong to our God”
paintings.poem:
the only place
in the whole New Testament
you'll find the word:
hallelujah.

four times,
in one chapter,
as if heaven
couldn't help itself.

save some of yours
for the end.
it's where
the word lives.

paintings.title: the wedding
paintings.epigraph: “Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb.”
paintings.poem:
the story that began in a garden
with a man and a woman

ends
at a wedding.

the Lamb and his bride—
all of us,
washed and dressed in white.

the table is long.
your name is on a chair.
you're invited.

paintings.title: Faithful and True
paintings.epigraph: “a white horse, and he who sat on it is called Faithful and True.”
paintings.poem:
the heavens open,
and here he comes.

not a new name.
the one he's always had:
Faithful.
True.

every promise in the book
was riding on that.

it still is.

paintings.title: the other book
paintings.epigraph: “Another book was opened, which is the book of life.”
paintings.poem:
the great and the small
stand before the throne,
and the books are opened.

everything we did,
written down.

and then—
another book.

the book of life.

in the end,
what matters most
isn't the record of our works.
it's whether our name
is written there.

paintings.title: no more sea
paintings.epigraph: “the sea is no more.”
paintings.poem:
a new heaven.
a new earth.
and no more sea.

for John,
the sea was the wall of his prison,
the water between him
and everyone he loved.

in the new world,
nothing
keeps us apart.

paintings.title: moving in
paintings.epigraph: “Behold, God’s dwelling is with people”
paintings.poem:
the tent in the desert.
the temple on the hill.
the Word who pitched his tent among us.

and now, at last:

God's home
is with people.

he doesn't visit.
he moves in
for good.

paintings.title: every tear
paintings.epigraph: “He will wipe away every tear from their eyes.”
paintings.poem:
not the tears of one bad day.
every tear.

the ones you cried alone.
the ones you swallowed.
the ones
you didn't know were still there.

God himself
will wipe them away,

and death,
and grief,
and crying,
and pain—

gone.
the first things
passed away.

paintings.title: all things new
paintings.epigraph: “Write, for these words of God are faithful and true.”
paintings.poem:
not all new things.
all things new.

he's not throwing the world away
and starting over.

he's making
this world,
these people,
your life,
new.

write it down,
he said.
it's true.

paintings.title: gates of pearl
paintings.epigraph: “The twelve gates were twelve pearls.”
paintings.poem:
a pearl
begins as an injury—
a grain of grit
the oyster couldn't get rid of,
wrapped in layer after layer.

and every gate
into the city of God
is a pearl.

the way in
was made
from a wound.

paintings.title: the lamp
paintings.epigraph: “its lamp is the Lamb.”
paintings.poem:
no sun.
no moon.
no need.

the glory of God
is the light,
and the Lamb
is the lamp.

the one who called himself
the light of the world
wasn't exaggerating.

paintings.title: leaves for healing
paintings.epigraph: “The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.”
paintings.poem:
the tree we lost
in the first garden—

here it is,
on both banks of the river,
fruit every month,

and leaves
for the healing of the nations.

the Bible ends
where it began:
a garden,
a river,
a tree,
and God.

paintings.title: come
paintings.epigraph: “He who is thirsty, let him come.”
paintings.poem:
the Spirit says: come.
the bride says: come.

whoever is thirsty,
come.

whoever wants it,
take the water of life—
free.

the last invitation
in the Bible
has no fine print.

paintings.title: come, Lord Jesus
paintings.epigraph: “Y es, come, Lord Jesus.”
paintings.poem:
yes, I am coming soon.

and the church
answers
with the oldest prayer we have:

come, Lord Jesus.

and then the last line
of the whole Bible
is not a warning,
not a vision,

but this:
grace
be with you all.
